She stepped into the dim light of the forest, where shadows danced beneath the towering trees, their leaves rustling gently in the cool breeze. A sense of weight settled upon her chest, the silence punctuated only by the distant call of a wood thrush, each note weaving through the stillness and pulling her deeper into the woods.

The way his dark hair fell into his eyes made her stomach twist with an unexpected flutter. How could he look so carefree when everything felt so heavy?

“Yeah, I’m coming,” she replied, brushing a stray twig off her jacket, her voice a touch sharper than she intended. She didn’t want him to see the uncertainty swirling inside her, the dread of what lay ahead.

Aiden pushed himself off the tree and started down the narrow path, the crunch of leaves underfoot echoing in the stillness. She followed, the forest swallowing their footsteps, the air thick with the scent of damp earth and decaying leaves.
